question.text: As Attorney General under his brother John, this man personally authorized some of the FBI's requests, including wiretapping phones to spy on Martin Luther King.
question.answerHtml: Robert Francis Kennedy (accept RFK; accept Bobby Kennedy; prompt on “Kennedy” alone)
question.clue: In televised hearings, this counsel for the Senate Labor Rackets Committee attempted to ruin Teamster union president Jimmy Hoffa.

swap.leadin: Give the following about lunar exploration.
swap.text: Every mission which put people on the moon was part of this NASA program; the 11th, 12th, and 14th through 17th missions of this name were successful at that goal
swap.clue: Gene Kranz aborted one of this program's missions, in which an oxygen tank explosion nearly killed James Lovell and his crew.

question.leadin: Give the following about containment, the official US policy for stopping the spread of communism.
question.text: This President, who served between Ford and Reagan, tried to shift from containment to a more pacifist foreign policy until the Soviets invaded Afghanistan in 1979. He won a Nobel Peace Prize in 2002, in part for his work with Habitat for Humanity.
question.clue: This President lost his reelection bid in a race that featured Independent candidate John B. Anderson.

swap.text: The Catholic Knights of Columbus lobbied the Eisenhower administration to add this controversial two-word phrase to the pledge. This phrase has come under fire for seemingly violating the First Amendment.
swap.clue: Because John Nicolay and John Hay's drafts omit this phrase, some people are skeptical that this two-word phrase was used before the words "shall have a new birth of freedom" in the last sentence of the Gettysburg Address.

question.text: The Tower Commission opened their report on this scandal with the Juvenal quote "Who watches the watchmen?" Fawn Hall testified against John Poindexter and Oliver North for their part in this scandal.
question.clue: Both John Poindexter and Caspar Weinberger were convicted after the investigation by the Tower Commission over this scandal, which involved violating the Boland Amendment and began as an arms-for-hostages deal.

swap.leadin: Name some things about the contentious nomination of Robert Bork to the Supreme Court.
swap.text: Within an hour of the nomination announcement, this long-serving senator from Massachusetts took to the Senate Floor to denounce it. He never secured the Democratic nomination for the presidency as a result of an incident at Chappaquiddick Creek.
swap.clue: This man pleaded guilty to leaving the scene of the crash during the Chappaquiddick ("Chap-uh-kwih-dihk") incident, which killed Mary Jo Kopechne ("kuh-pehk-nee").

question.leadin: Identify some candidates from the 1964 U.S. Presidential election.
question.text: Nicknamed "Mr. Conservative," this Republican from Texas became the primary opponent of LBJ, but that's not saying much as he lost a very lopsided election.
question.clue: He was harmed by a message which ended "We must love one another, or we must die" after zooming in on the eye of a figure who skips the number six and repeats the number nine twice in trying to count to ten.

swap.leadin: This man served as both President of Columbia University and President of the United States.
swap.text: Name this man who was the Supreme Commander of the Allied Forces in Europe during World War II and whose vice president was Richard Nixon. He was succeeded by John F. Kennedy.
swap.clue: Another speech by this leader warned against the "grave implications" of an "acquisition of unwarranted influence" in the "councils of government."

question.leadin: Kevin Phillips, a strategist for this president, outlined a plan for beating the Democrats by appealing to Catholics and Southerners in "The Emerging Republican Majority"
question.text: Identify this president who made a historical visit to China with his wife, Pat.
question.clue: A ruling in which this man was the respondent cited Accardi v. Shaughnessy to assert the power of the Attorney General and notes that "in camera inspection" is not a substantial diminishment of communications.

swap.leadin: This event led to the resignations of Elliot Richardson and William Ruckelshaus.
swap.text: Name this event in which Richard Nixon fired special prosecutor Archibald Cox.
swap.clue: The target of this event was offered the Stennis Compromise by its instigator.

question.text: During the trial, Dan White's lawyer's citing of his junk food eating habits as a sign of his depression was misleadingly dubbed a "defense" named for this sugary snack food.
question.clue: Bill Clinton put one of these food items in the official White House Millennium Time Capsule.

swap.text: This conservative political activist and opponent of the Equal Rights Amendment wrote the book A Choice, Not an Echo in support of the Goldwater campaign. Today, she gives lectures and maintains a website that argues that a North American Union in parallel with the European Union would be a bad idea.
swap.clue: This person likened "using an atomic bomb to exterminate mice" to legislation sponsored by Michigan representative Martha Griffiths.

question.text: Rockefeller was appointed to the Vice-Presidency after the ascension of this man. According to Hunter S. Thompson, this man declared that "I know I will go to hell, because I pardoned Richard Nixon."
question.answerHtml: Gerald Rudolph Ford, Jr. [or Leslie Lynch King, Jr.]
question.clue: This man promised to "Whip Inflation Now" and was president during the fall of Saigon.

swap.text: Although Shockley was a terrible boss, he shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics with John Bardeen and Walter Brattain for inventing these devices.

question.text: This historian ended up on the enemies list after he attacked Nixon in The Imperial Presidency. This former special assistant to JFK glorified the Kennedy presidency in his book A Thousand Days.
question.answerHtml: Arthur Schlesinger Jr. [do not accept or prompt on “Arthur Schlesinger Sr.”]
question.clue: This Pulitzer-prize winning historian of The Imperial Presidency detailed the controversy of JFK needing voter support from McCarthy supporters in his book A Thousand Days.

swap.text: The United States entered the Vietnam War after a 1964 incident in which the USS Maddox and Turner Joy were attacked in what body of water?
swap.clue: In this body of water, the Maddox was attacked by the North Vietnamese during an intelligence mission; this incident would eventually lead to escalation of American involvement in Vietnam.

question.leadin: Pat Manion convinced Leo Brent Bozell, the brother-in-law of William F. Buckley Jr., to ghostwrite this political manifesto for a man that Bozell would later serve as speechwriter.
question.text: Name this 1960 book published under the name of future presidential candidate Barry Goldwater.

swap.leadin: Captained by Charles Miller, it was boarded on May 12th by Khmer Rouge forces while en route to Thailand.
swap.text: Name this merchant vessel that caused a crisis during the Ford administration when the U.S. decided on a swift military rescue as the best possibility.
swap.clue: During Ford's presidency, Cambodia seized this U.S. merchant ship. The 41 marines killed during the rescue operation of this ship are the last to appear on the Vietnam Veterans Memorial.

question.text: Anti-Warren and anti-UN signs decorated the Dallas yard of this far-right activist. Lee Harvey Oswald attempted to assassinate this former general, who was forced to resign after trying to train his troops with John Birch pamphlets.

swap.leadin: This senator sponsored the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938, and exempted insurance companies from antitrust law in a doubly-eponymous act with Homer Ferguson.
swap.text: Name this notoriously anti-semetic senator, nicknamed the "Senator from Madrid" due to his unyielding support of Francisco Franco. He sponsored a namesake Internal Security Act.
